items.title: A simple request for AI to book a gym class exposed a major threat
items.description: When Andrew asked his AI personal assistant to book him a spot in a gym class, he had no idea he would accidentally initiate an autonomous cyber attack.

items.title: Frydenberg says he will not be called as royal commission witness
items.description: Former treasurer Josh Frydenberg said he made a submission to the commission and indicated his willingness to appear as a witness.

items.title: ICAC questions lobbyist's role with 'toxic' Reformers
items.description: Lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood said a right-wing Liberal Party factional group at the centre of a corruption watchdog inquiry became so "toxic" he encouraged his friends to leave it.

items.title: Sydney Airport near miss 'could have been far more serious', ATSB boss says
items.description: Australian Transport Safety Bureau's Chief Commissioner Angus Mitchell says pilots who avoided a near miss at Sydney Airport on Sunday morning "prevented what could have been far more serious".

items.title: Police believe 'body' found in suitcase by road was a sex doll
items.description: Police sources say a "body" found in a suitcase in southern NSW is believed to be a sex doll, rather than the remains of a woman as first feared.

items.title: Deluge halts footy and washes cars away in SA
items.description: Heavy rainfall across South Australia stopped a weekend football match, while three people were rescued from their vehicles after attempting to drive through floodwaters.

items.title: A golden mic, a 'clunky start' but Sandilands returns to the air
items.description: Described by the shock jock himself as a "digital mess" Kyle Sandilands has launched his new show with NSW Premier Chris Minns his first guest.

items.title: Geelong Cats board holds crisis meeting over concussion deal
items.description: Geelong is about to reply to the AFL's please explain as the Cats brace for a potential massive penalty over the secret concussion deal with Jake Kolodjashnij.

items.title: Australia has the most expensive cigarettes in the world, and now a booming black market
items.description: After decades as a world leader in tobacco control, Australia now finds itself in troubled waters. But those trying to find solutions are far from on the same page.

items.title: Live: PM flags action on inducements to win Coalition support for gambling laws
items.description: Anthony Albanese has flagged action on gambling advertisement inducements that could likely result in the Coalition's support of the government's proposed reforms. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese is the opposite of Rudd and that comes with its own risks
items.description: Cabinet's indecision on support for Tony Burke's immigration cuts shows a key difference between Anthony Albanese and Kevin Rudd.

items.title: Accused Chinese people smuggler denied bail in Cairns court
items.description: An alleged people smuggler is denied bail after his fishing-trip alibi was dismissed because he had 10 illegal migrants in his hotel room and no evidence of an interest in fishing.

items.title: Israeli government rejects Trump's Gaza peace plan
items.description: Israeli Prime Minster Benjamin Netanyahu says Hamas's proposed plan for disarming is "unacceptable", rejecting the Trump administration's plans to end fighting in the Palestinian territory.

items.title: How Elliot won Race Around the World in 'opportunity of a lifetime'
items.description: After 100 days making films in different countries, Race Around the World winner Elliot Constable credits one particular approach for his success.

items.title: What are the rules for taking carer's leave from work?
items.description: When it comes to taking time off work for your own personal illness or injury, you probably have some idea of what your entitlements are. But when it comes to needing time off to care for others, you may be more unsure of your rights.

items.title: History quiz: Show us what you know about 90s pop culture and musical masterpieces
items.description: We'll also test you on the Paris Olympics, the 2017 parliamentary citizenship scandal and history-making Test cricket.

items.title: The end of the low interest rate era is here and it weighs on house prices
items.description: We seem to have flipped from worrying about rising house prices to worrying about falling house prices. Well, some of us have, anyway.

items.title: Millions of Australians could have no say in who inherits their super
items.description: New research shows most Australians have not made a legally binding death benefit nomination to ensure their superannuation goes to who they want it to when they die. And many funds do not make it easy.

items.title: Child safety worker union alarmed by possible removal of key reporting tool
items.description: The union representing child safety workers in Queensland has highlighted concerns about the possible removal of a key reporting tool.

items.title: Australia's 'FIFO ghosts' a growing problem on census night
items.description: Mining cities across Australia say the count fails to acknowledge the increasing pressure the nation's growing fly-in fly-out workforce puts on communities.

items.title: Big changes for NSW renters as portable bond scheme begins
items.description: The NSW government's portable rental bond system starts today and will cost renters who want to use the online service $25.

items.title: Regional emergency departments a 'basket case of mania', doctor warns
items.description: The most dysfunctional emergency departments in Victoria are in regional areas, according to data, with doctors describing overcrowded corridors, lapses in patient safety and burnt-out staff.

items.title: Brazilian footballer falls in tunnel after scoring disallowed goal
items.description: A Brazilian footballer has fallen into a stadium tunnel after celebrating a goal before it was disallowed. Almost a decade ago, another footballer fell into the same tunnel.

items.title: Who killed Tupac? Three decades later, there may finally be answers
items.description: Three decades after the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, the world may get some answers about who killed the young superstar, and why.

items.title: Zelenskyy says 50,000 North Korean troops will help Russia in war
items.description: Mr Zelenskyy took to social media to announced that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", while calling on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine's air defence.
